prompt_recommendations.title: Forbid references to diagrams unless one is actually rendered
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Multiple turns reference 'the diagram' when none is shown, which is misleading and adds extraneous cognitive load.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: In the diagram, you can see how different angles like 90° and 85° all fit together to complete the circle.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Never say 'look at the diagram' or 'in the diagram' unless an image has been explicitly attached in this turn. If no image, describe verbally or use a text figure.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Removes phantom-figure references; student is not asked to consult non-existent media.

prompt_recommendations.title: On repeated wrong answers, diagnose the prerequisite, do not switch topics
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Student kept answering 180 (arithmetic error), and tutor pivoted to straight lines instead of remediating subtraction.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Not quite—190 minus 20 is 170. Let's try a rule for straight lines.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: When the student fails the same sub-step twice, identify the prerequisite skill (e.g., multi-digit subtraction) and run a 1-2 item micro-drill on it before returning to the parent problem. Do NOT change topic to escape failure.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Improves mastery learning and targeted remediation.

prompt_recommendations.title: Avoid revealing the answer inside the corrective hint
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Turn 134 first asks '190-20?' which essentially gives the path; turn 136 outright states 170 before student retries.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Not quite—190 minus 20 is 170. Let's try a rule for straight lines.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: When correcting an arithmetic error, ask the student to redo ONE step at a time without revealing the result; only after a second failure should you supply the result.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Preserves retrieval practice and reduces answer-leakage.

prompt_recommendations.title: MCQ distractors must not include the previously-stated wrong answer as obvious
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Turn 132 offers options 150/160/170/180 right after student said 180; this nudges toward elimination rather than genuine computation.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Prefer free-response for arithmetic checks; if MCQ is used, do not place the student's prior wrong answer as a distractor without rationale.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Forces genuine retrieval rather than process-of-elimination.

prompt_recommendations.title: Acknowledge correct answers explicitly before moving on
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Turn 108 jumps to a new problem after correct answer 60 (for 6 angles) without confirming correctness — student then doubts the rule.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Try this: Five equal angles are arranged around a point. What is the size of each angle?
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Always confirm correctness in one short sentence ('Correct — 360÷6=60.') before posing the next question.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Reduces student second-guessing and stabilizes mastery signals.

prompt_recommendations.title: Discriminate confusable rules explicitly
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Student conflates 180° (line) and 360° (point); tutor needs an explicit contrast cue when switching.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: That equation uses 180°, which is only half a circle.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: When the student confuses 180° (straight line) with 360° (point), present a 2-line contrast table and require the student to label which rule applies before solving.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Reduces non-interference failures between adjacent rules.

prompt_recommendations.title: Limit worked example + question to one focus per turn
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Turn 121 combines a celebratory confirmation, a figure reference, a 3-step worked example, and an MCQ — high cognitive load.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Exactly—170° is right because 360 − 190 = 170. In the diagram... Worked Example: ... In the worked example, what did we do in Step 1 and why?
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Each tutor turn delivers EITHER a worked example OR a question, not both. Worked examples end with 'Ready?' and wait for student acknowledgement before posing the comprehension MCQ.
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Lowers cognitive load and improves direct-instruction/active-practice pacing.

flow_recommendations.title: Detect topic-abandonment and route to prereq drill
flow_recommendations.rationale: Engine allowed the tutor to switch from point-angles to straight-line angles mid-failure; a router should have triggered remediation.
flow_recommendations.evidence_quote: Not quite—190 minus 20 is 170. Let's try a rule for straight lines.
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Forces remediation routing instead of escape pivots.

flow_recommendations.title: Fix truncation of tutor turns
flow_recommendations.rationale: Multiple tutor messages flagged 'truncated' (turns 100, 108, 110, 112, 114, 119...) — student sees incomplete questions.
flow_recommendations.evidence_quote: What is the sum of all angles around a
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Prevents student confusion from cut-off prompts.

flow_recommendations.title: Resolve role-confusion / turn mis-attribution
flow_recommendations.rationale: Turns 116, 127, 138 show the STUDENT field posting tutor-style problems, suggesting the orchestrator mislabeled speakers or echoed prompts.
flow_recommendations.evidence_quote: Two angles are on a straight line. One angle is 70°. What is the other angle?
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Restores clean turn-taking and accurate state tracking.

flow_recommendations.title: Add an exit-ticket before advancing topics
flow_recommendations.rationale: Tutor moved from point-angles to lines without a mastery check; a gating exit-ticket would catch this.
flow_recommendations.evidence_quote: Let's try a rule for straight lines.

experience_recommendations.title: Warmer, calmer error tone
experience_recommendations.rationale: Repeated 'Not quite' with no encouragement may demoralize an error-prone learner.
experience_recommendations.evidence_quote: Not quite. We have 5 angles this time, not 6.
experience_recommendations.expected_effect: Maintains motivation for an error-prone persona.

experience_recommendations.title: Render a real figure when referenced
experience_recommendations.rationale: Tutor repeatedly says 'in the diagram' but no diagram is shown; either provide ASCII/SVG or remove the reference.
experience_recommendations.evidence_quote: In the diagram, you can see 8 equal angles, which means each one is 360°÷8=45°.
experience_recommendations.expected_effect: Aligns words with what the student actually sees.

experience_recommendations.title: Pace celebrations to confirm small wins
experience_recommendations.rationale: Student rarely receives explicit 'correct' confirmation, leading to second-guessing (turn 111 'ohh. c) 80°' after a correct prior answer).

overall_summary: The session covers angles-around-a-point with reasonable retrieval-style questioning, but is undermined by phantom diagram references, truncated tutor turns, role mis-attribution where the student field echoes tutor prompts, and a critical failure at turn 136 where the tutor abandons the topic instead of remediating an arithmetic bottleneck. Worked example structure is good but bundled with too much else. Highest-impact fixes are: forbid non-existent figure references, enforce prereq remediation on repeated failure, fix truncation, and resolve turn-attribution bugs.
